key_insight: A query-only LLM audit closely reproduced clinical prediction models and detected nearly all planted flaws, but its additional warnings and discoveries required verification.
clinical_relevance: LLM-assisted audits could support scrutiny of clinical prediction tools, but these results do not establish safety or improved patient outcomes.
method: Trained four model types on International Stroke Trial data for two outcomes.
Mixed 24 deliberately flawed models with 8 clean models.
GPT-6 Astra audited each model three times using prediction queries alone, with blinded, precommitted scoring.
evidence_signal: Surrogates achieved mean log-odds R² of 0.976 and audits detected 69/72 planted flaws (96%; 95% CI 80–99%), while a purpose-written script detected all 24 flawed models.
watch_item: Extra findings need independent checks: 60% of checkable problem reports failed the prespecified test, and only 11% of unexpected relationships from clean models held in later-randomised patients.
paper_title: Auditing black-box clinical prediction models with a large language model through queries alone: a blinded test with planted flaws
